title: (Backwards) Into the Future: Nostalgic and Anticipated Deprivation as Predictors of Populist Voting in a Two-Wave Election Study
abstract: Abstract: While populist voting is often explained by perceiving one’s group as unfairly worse off than others ( collective relative deprivation), the group’s past and future may provide further politically consequential benchmarks for deprivation. Using two-wave panel data from the East German state election Study 2024, we find that nostalgic and anticipated deprivation are strongly correlated and independently predict far-right populist voting beyond collective relative deprivation. In contrast, left-wing populist voting was negatively predicted by nostalgic deprivation, positively by collective relative deprivation, and unrelated to anticipated deprivation. Following the election, anticipated deprivation decreased among far-right voters, while changes varied with perceived electoral success. These findings broaden the temporal lens on relative deprivation, highlighting how perceived status trajectories relate to present-day populist support.
